artists.biography:
Porcupine Tree are a rock band formed by Steven Wilson in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, England. Their music is associated with both psychedelic rock and progressive rock, yet having been influenced by trance, krautrock and ambient due to Steven Wilson and Richard Barbieri's penchant for the Kosmische Musik scene of the early 1970s, led by bands such as Tangerine Dream, Neu! and Can. Since the early 2000s (decade), their music has been leaning towards progressive metal and alternative rock.
The band is noted for its multimedia approach, with its live performances including screens displaying a different film projection to each song. This visual element was introduced during the tour for the In Absentia album, when the band started to work with Danish photographer and filmmaker Lasse Hoile. This involvement created a distinctive image for the band.
Despite being signed to both Roadrunner and Atlantic labels, the band has their own record label, Transmission, which they use to launch some independent releases and special editions of their albums. In 2007 the band was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Surround Sound Album with their album Fear of a Blank Planet and then again in 2010 with The Incident.
Music Radar website placed them amongst "The 30 greatest live acts in the world today" (as of 2010), coming at number 4.

lastfm.wiki_content: On The Sunday Of Life... is the debut album of English progressive rock band Porcupine Tree, first released in July, 1991. It compiles tracks that Steven Wilson produced and recorded for two cassette-only releases, Tarquin's Seaweed Farm (1989) and The Nostalgia Factory (1990). This first real album contained a lot of peculiar material, but also tracks that would grow to be among the group's classic songs (particularly "Radioactive Toy"). Most of the lyrics were written by Alan Duffy, a school friend with whom Steven Wilson had lost touch a few years before the album was released. A small run of 1000 copies in a deluxe gatefold sleeve was released in early 1992. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
On the Sunday of Life... is Porcupine Tree’s debut album, assembled from material Steven Wilson had originally recorded for the cassette-era releases Tarquin’s Seaweed Farm and The Nostalgia Factory. Issued by Delerium Records in 1992, it presents the project in its earliest form: a sprawling, home-studio collection of psychedelic rock, space rock, and progressive rock ideas, with a strong experimental bent and a loose, exploratory feel.

The album is notable for introducing several traits that would define Porcupine Tree’s later work, including immersive atmospheres, melodic guitar passages, and a fondness for oddball titles and transitional pieces. Its centerpiece “Radioactive Toy” became a fan favorite, and the record’s mix of ambient drift, psychedelic textures, and occasional hooks earned it a cult following, especially after the limited initial pressing sold well enough to keep it in circulation.

Though rougher and more eccentric than the band’s later, more refined albums, On the Sunday of Life... has remained important as the document of Porcupine Tree’s beginnings and as an early statement of Steven Wilson’s solo-driven vision. It is often viewed as a curiosity by some listeners, but also as an essential first chapter in the group’s evolution.
